question.problem: If $u=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ k \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 1 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal vectors, then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =(-2)\cdot k+0\cdot 1+k\cdot 5+3\cdot (-2) \\  & =-2k+0+5k-6 \\  & =3k-6\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}3k-6 & =0 \\ 3k & =6 \\ k & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
